title: Apollo 17 lunar module powered descent, reference track

clock.ignition_note: Mission Report (JSC-07904 table 8-VI) ignition 110:09:53 = 112:49:53 ALSJ clock. ALSJ text says 112:49:56 (3 s later); unresolved, MR used because contact 113:01:58 matches MR 110:21:58 and MR lists ignition-to-landing 12:05 = 725 s.
clock.t_definition: t_s = seconds since DPS ignition on the Mission Report clock (110:09:53 MR = 112:49:53 ALSJ). get_mr_s / get_alsj_s are GET seconds on the two clocks; utc = launch 1972-12-07T05:33:00Z + get_mr_s.

frame.origin: the Apollo 17 lunar module rest position (Haase LROC control point + patch shift +12.7 E / +7.2 N, src/ground/site17.ts), at ground level
frame.axes: east, north, up at the origin, metres; the origin MOVES with the Moon (ground-fixed), so E,N,U and velocities are ground-relative. U is height above the TANGENT PLANE at the origin (negative and large far away: -61 km at PDI); alt_m is height above the local ground (site radius) as called by the crew.
frame.attitude: quat_wxyz rotates body (X forward through the windows, Y left, Z up along the descent-engine thrust axis, right-handed) into ENU. psi_deg = angle of the thrust axis from local vertical, tilted AGAINST the flight direction (ALSJ pitch, 0 = vertical; 108 at ignition). yaw_left_deg = rotation about the thrust axis (MR yaw 290 = 70 left). roll is 0 before contact (est). heading_deg = compass bearing of the forward axis, nose_elev_deg = its elevation (past 90 the nose points over the zenith: windows up).
frame.g1_conversion: G1 model space (lmPlacement.ts attitudeQuat) is three axes (east, up, south) with model +z front, +y up, +x left: three.x = E, three.y = U, three.z = -N; model (x,y,z) = (left, up, forward).

provenance_codes.V: verified table or text value read in this session (source in waypoints.json)
provenance_codes.R: read second-hand or from a summary, not re-checked at source
provenance_codes.I: interpolated between V/R waypoints by monotone PCHIP
provenance_codes.E: estimated by the model, band given

columns_doc: one entry per second, t_s from 0 (ignition) to 732 (5 s after engine stop); parallel arrays. prov.* and unc.* give the tag and band of each value group.

events.event: ignition, DPS at minimum throttle (10 percent)

events.src: MR table 8-VI 110:11:25 (its T+ column reads 00:32, an OCR/misprint; 110:11:25 - 110:09:53 = 1:32). ALSJ puts the Houston call at 112:51:03 (T+1:07 on its clock); text says about 2 min in

events.event: P66 landing phase (manual attitude/rate, just under 300 ft per MR)

events.src: MR: total firing about 727 s => 2 s after contact; ALSJ has engine stop about 113:02:03 (5 s). Band +2..+5 s.

table.src: ALSJ call altitude; time est between 200 ft@113:00:55 and 80 ft@113:01:15

table.what: 'getting a little dust' (ALSJ table); MR: first observed at 60 to 70 ft on the tape meter
dust becomes easily visible in the film (ALSJ commentary at about 113:01:38)
table.prov: V for the film time, E for the height

table.what: contact light; MR: landing radar had no lock-up on moving dust

dust_and_contact.rendering_index: dust_index in powered{} is a 0..1 rendering scale interpolated over the call table: 0 above 110 ft, 0.12 at 80 ft, 0.2 at 65 ft (MR: first seen 60 to 70 ft), 0.3 at 40 ft, 0.5 at 35 ft (film: easily visible), 1.0 at contact. E. Not a physical dust density. The MR says the radar did not lock onto dust.
dust_and_contact.contact_probes_prov: R (60 in on Apollo 16 and 17, web summary of collectSPACE/Wikipedia; not read at source)
dust_and_contact.contact_light: lit when a probe tip touches, so at contact the pad plane is about probe-length above the ground; alt_m is 0 there, pad_alt_m is the pad plane height
dust_and_contact.engine_bell_height: UNKNOWN in the sources read; needs the LM-12 descent-stage drawing (the J-mission extended skirt). No number given.
dust_and_contact.thrust_near_contact: throttle_of_ftp and thrust_N are E; at contact the thrust is about hover weight (mass * lunar g)
dust_and_contact.landing_gear: MR: rear strut rested near the bottom of a 3 to 4 m crater, attitude after shutdown 4 to 5 deg pitch up and 0 roll, near zero yaw (ALSJ adds about 2 deg left roll); harder-than-anticipated aft impact: pivot on the forward strut.

touchdown.origin_lonlat_haase_plus_shift: origin = LM_HAASE (30.7716815 E, 20.1909097 N) + 12.7 m E, +7.2 N (patch frame, see site17.ts)

mr_photomap_coordinates.note: MR 20 09 55 N, 30 45 57 E on the 1:25,000 Taurus-Littrow photomap; before the LROC controlled position, so about 0.8 km SSW of the Haase position

target_offset_records.brief: landing about 230 m W and 60 m S of the target; target = LM + (230 E, 60 N)
target_offset_records.mr: eight redesignations, ending several hundred metres south of the targeted point (Mission Report 10.7); +3400 ft downrange target update early in the burn
target_offset_records.alsj: planned point about 230 m west and about 60 m south of the actual landing site, as fetched (direction wording ambiguous in the fetch summary, not re-read in the original)

sun.source: src/ephemeris.ts (astronomy-engine), site lon/lat from scripts/sites.json a17

shadow_of_H_m.prov: H is R (LM overall height 7.04 m; not read here)

alsj_reference.note: brief: real landing Sun about 14 deg east (elevation), LM shadow 33.5 m west; ALSJ postland page (fetched) says the LM shadow was about 100 ft (30 m)

facts: Ignition: yaw 70 deg left, thrust axis 108 deg from vertical (pointing east, 18 deg below the horizon), windows face the sky (crew on their backs, heads east).
Yaw 70 -> 20 left at 112:54:07 (MR: 290 -> 340 with landing radar lock); yaw 0 at about 112:56:33, "windows up" (ALSJ). The Earth was in the front window at 112:55:04 and left it at 112:56:33.
During the braking phase the forward axis is elevated 74 deg (5:08) to 60 deg (8:21) above the horizon toward the flight direction: the windows show sky, not ground.

Pitchover at 112:59:15 (P64): psi 60 -> about 20; the surface comes into the window ("filled the window"), South Massif visible out the bottom of the commander window at 13,000 ft (MR) / 16,000 ft (ALSJ 112:58:17).
Final approach: near vertical (psi about 0 by 680 s in the fit, E), windows look west, forward and down through the lower part of the window (MR: extra effort to look out the bottom half).
Rest: nose 4.5 deg up, left roll 2 deg (heading is not in the sources; ALSJ: 12 oclock is due west on approach).
window_geometry.prov: V for the attitude angles at waypoints, E after the pitchover

estimated_or_unknown: Horizontal velocity and downrange at every time: E (model, bands in unc.v_horizontal_ms / unc.pos_E_m from the ensemble in checks.ensemble). Not in any source read.
Approach-phase pitch history 577..725 s: E (three fitted values, checks.fit). Only "60 -> about 20 deg" at pitchover and "about zero at shutdown" are sourced.

Pre-PDI crossrange and orbit plane: E (plane through the site containing due west at the site; the orbit inclination follows, about the site latitude). The Mission Report tables were not found for the ground track.
PDI altitude 8.7 nmi: R (search summary of the Mission Report, not in the text layer I read).
Thrust 9,710 lbf and the min throttle 1,050 lbf: E (published values, not in the report); the fit changes the full thrust by under 1 percent.
Engine-stop time (+2 s MR, +5 s ALSJ), pad touchdown time (free fall from probe length), engine bell height: E / unknown.
ALSJ clock vs MR clock: ignition 3 s apart (112:49:56 vs 112:49:53).
Moon rotation is included (site moves east 4.3 m/s inertially); libration and gravity harmonics are not.
